system_description.narrative_title: Fractured Interdependence: Tech, Oil and War Reshaping the Global Order
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly coupled system in flux where regional wars (notably Iran‑US/Hormuz and Russia‑Ukraine), a geopolitically charged tech-industrial race, and stressed energy and food supply chains interact to produce cascading economic and security shocks. Central banks and markets oscillate in response to inflation data and commodity volatility while states and corporations deploy industrial policy, finance and military measures to hedge risk and seize advantage. Climate extremes, migration pressures and novel private‑sector roles (AI financing, space, private cyber operations) add nonlinear stresses that reconfigure alliances and domestic politics across regions.
system_description.scope: Nation-states and alliances; regional conflicts and security operations; global financial markets and central banks; energy, shipping and commodity supply chains; major technology firms and industrial policy; migration flows and domestic political responses; climate-driven resource shocks; non-state armed groups and private military/cyber actors.

variables.name: Strait of Hormuz standoff
variables.description: The United States, Iran and Gulf states are locked in a standoff over control and security of the Strait of Hormuz, driving recurring attacks, diplomatic deadlock and sustained oil-market disruption.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine remain engaged in high-intensity conflict, with shifting front lines, strikes on ports and infrastructure and cascading impacts on food, energy and regional security.

variables.name: US–China tech and AI rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are contesting dominance in semiconductors, AI, data and finance through export controls, industrial policy and investment campaigns that are reshaping global supply chains and capital flows.

variables.name: China maritime militarisation and Taiwan pressure
variables.description: China’s growing naval and missile activities around Taiwan and the wider Indo-Pacific are increasing military friction with Taiwan, Japan, Southeast Asian states and the United States, altering regional deterrence dynamics.

variables.name: Global monetary and inflation stress
variables.description: Major central banks and currency blocs (Fed, BOJ, ECB, others) are navigating persistent inflation, rising bond yields and episodic currency interventions, producing renewed market volatility and shifts in capital allocation.
